correctness.rationale: For each n>=1 and k>=3, occurrence-order rank permutations coincide. The absence of nested a,b,b,a or b,a,a,b subsequences forces for consecutive letters a_i,a_{i+1} the inequalities p_(a_i,k-1)<p_(a_(i+1),1) and p_(a_i,k)<p_(a_(i+1),2), leaving exactly independently swappable adjacent block-boundary pairs. For a base word sigma_1^k...sigma_n^k the only existing descents are at positions ki corresponding to descents of sigma. Each boundary swap increases descent count by one and major index by exactly ki: for ascending a<b introduces descent at ki; for descending a>b replaces descent ki with ki-1 and ki+1. Neighbourhoods are disjoint for k>=3. Summing over B and sigma proves A_n(u,q^k)product(1+u q^(ki)). MacMahon specialization then gives the full multiples-of-k support and palindromicity. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all multiset words (rather than the bundled lattice-word code) for n=2,k=3,4 and n=3,k=3 recovered 4,4,24 admissible words and all bivariate terms. The all-parameter proof is structural; no finite extrapolation.
